rationale: PINS RULE R7's EMPTY-NAME half, found by the census endpoint count rather than by reading: 1 edge with an empty target in 500 corpus files, and it was the only empty endpoint in any of the ten types (measured over the 2,000-file draw: `references` 1, every other type 0). The shape is `src/cmd/compile/internal/syntax/testdata/tparams.go` verbatim — `func f[ /* ERROR empty type parameter list */ ]()`. The pinned grammar types that hole as a `type_identifier` whose `text` is the empty string; the declared-type collector took it like any other type name and published `references f -> ""`, an endpoint no declaration can resolve and no consumer can navigate to. The guard refuses a nameless node INSIDE the collector rather than at the push site, because the collector is the only place that can tell a recovered hole from a written name. THE FILE DOES NOT COMPILE and is a file of its own for that reason: a recovery fixture sharing a file with compilable pins would weaken them, which is why the lane's round-5 fixture moved its two recovery shapes into a probe. The EXPECT rows are the over-application control — `Recovered`'s damaged list still publishes its two surviving type parameters, and `WithMethods -> Recovered` still publishes, so a guard that dropped the whole list instead of the empty name fails here. The `target: ""` forbid row is a lane-wide statement of the invariant rather than of this one shape, which is deliberate: it is the only row in the fixture format that can say 'no edge of this type may have an empty endpoint'.
